args.name: --collection
args.help: search one collection only (filtered before the top-k cut)

args.name: --limit
args.help: return at most N hits (default 10; a cut is always disclosed)

args.name: --all
args.help: no cut on the lexical arms: rank every FTS match (exclusive with --limit)

hints: Ranked file#heading hits with an FTS5 snippet excerpt (keyword + graph, +vectors if PLAINKEEP_VECTORS). `--author human` excludes agent + derived material; `--author agent` keeps only agent notes (provenance planes). `--collection wiki|tasks|journal|inbox` searches one collection only (every hit carries its `collection`). `--limit N` / `--all` set the cap (default 10); a truncated result says so: the human output ends with `showing N of ≥M — use --limit/--all` and `--json` adds `returned`, `limit`, `truncated` and `lexical_total` (the exact count of FTS-matching notes) to the header line. For "everything with this tag" use `plainkeep wiki list --tag <tag>`, not search. `--open` jumps to the top hit via `plainkeep open`; bare `plainkeep search` in a tty with fzf opens a live search session. Common mistake: running before `plainkeep index`, or too narrow a query — broaden and reindex.
